newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit loses gains as dlr selling from KL eases.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit loses gains as dlr selling from KL eases.

text.p: The ringgit lost its early gains as dollar sales from Kuala Lumpur eased in the afternoon and offshore funds continued selling the Malaysian unit, dealers said on Thursday.
They said early sales of the U.S. unit by Malaysian utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd, which has recently accumulated dollars from a Yankee bond issue, had helped the ringgit.
"It has been selling in small quantities. But, the effect was exaggerated," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
"I don't see dollar/ringgit moving out of the 2.4900/5050 range in the near-term," the dealer said.
Dealers said offshore funds were still holding large short ringgit positions. "The sentiment is still for a slight weakening of the ringgit," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
But, some dealers said with the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee not announcing any interest rate hike on Tuesday, there was a possibility of some funds returning to Malaysia.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5007/17 a dollar.
